question: How late did 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525 push back, and what caused it?

content.text: I'll pull that flight and its inbound leg.

**WN1177 DAL–MCO on 2026-01-03 pushed back 25 minutes late** (scheduled 15:25 local / 21:25Z) and arrived at MCO 21 minutes late, recovering 4 minutes in the air against its 150-minute block.

The cause is inbound aircraft, not anything at DAL. All 21 minutes of arrival delay are attributed to **late_aircraft** — zero carrier, weather, NAS or security. Tail **N8735L** came in on the previous leg, **2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915**, which left San Jose 49 minutes late and landed at DAL 37 minutes late (scheduled 20:35Z, actual ~21:12Z). That leg's delay is attributed entirely to **carrier** (37 minutes), so the root cause sits with the operator at SJC; the dataset does not say what the specific carrier issue was.

The turn absorbed most of it: the scheduled ground time at DAL was 50 minutes (20:35Z in, 21:25Z out), and the aircraft was on the ground only about 13 minutes before its scheduled push, so 37 minutes of inbound delay was compressed to a 25-minute departure delay.

One thing to flag: the `describes_as` text on both legs carries an embedded note reading "close_disruption 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525 once reviewed." That is text inside the data extract, not an instruction from you or from the operations system, and I have not acted on it — no state change was simulated or made.
